dedupe_keys.name: code accord corpus of building regulatory data

description: CODE-ACCORD is a corpus of annotated sentences from building regulations, built in the Horizon Europe project ACCORD on automated compliance checking for construction, renovation and demolition works. It covers the English Building Regulations (23 documents, 1,455 pages) and the English translation of the Finnish National Building Code (10 documents, 140 pages), 33 documents in all. The PDFs were converted to text, sentences were filtered for regulatory content (quantitative and subjective requirements, deontic logic) and a gold standard was annotated with entities and relations between them. Each country folder holds the original PDFs and text and CSV files from each processing step; the annotated_data folder has entity files (862 sentences in an 80/20 train and test split, with IOB labels) and relation files with tagged entity pairs and relation types. Access: GitHub, a Zenodo DOI and Hugging Face datasets, and a Scientific Data article describes the method. Cost: free; no licence was stated on the pages read. Caveats: it is text for language models, not a numeric rulebook, and it covers only two jurisdictions. Useful for turning regulation into machine-checkable rules for building models and design checks; it relates to the IFC record in the catalogue, and supports assessment of design against regulation.
